subject.title: Feature Request: Support YAML as config file format

question: Should OpenClaw keep JSON5 `openclaw.json` as the only core config file format, or should it accept YAML/YML config files as a second core config contract?
rationale: This is not a broken existing behavior; it changes config loading, writing, docs, and upgrade expectations in a stable core surface, and repository policy makes config-surface expansion a maintainer product decision.

options.title: Keep JSON5 Canonical
options.body: Reaffirm `openclaw.json` plus `openclaw config`/`config.patch` as the supported path and consider a small docs improvement for comment-safe programmatic edits.

options.title: Approve YAML As Second Format
options.body: Define precedence when multiple files exist, parser semantics, write-back behavior, reload behavior, docs, tests, and any doctor migration before implementation.

options.title: Defer Until More Demand
options.body: Leave the issue open as a product backlog item and ask for concrete workflows where existing config CLI, `config.patch`, or `oc-path` cannot cover the need.

recommendation.title: Keep JSON5 Canonical
recommendation.body: Reaffirm `openclaw.json` plus `openclaw config`/`config.patch` as the supported path and consider a small docs improvement for comment-safe programmatic edits.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest recent history signal across the config path/parser/writer files and docs touched by this product choice.
